/-!
# Conjecture 4.13

by Ya. G. Berkovich

Prove that every finite non-abelian $p$-group admits an automorphism of order $p$
which is not an inner one.

Here the inner automorphisms of $G$ are the conjugation maps $x \mapsto g x g^{-1}$
for $g \in G$, i.e. the range of `MulAut.conj : G →* MulAut G`. The automorphism is
required to have order exactly $p$ in $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

    ∃ φ : MulAut G, orderOf φ = p ∧ φ ∉ (MulAut.conj : G →* MulAut G).range := by

theorem kourovka.«4.13» (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G]

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified assertion: for every prime p and every finite non-abelian p-group G there exists φ ∈ Aut(G) with orderOf φ = p exactly (not merely a p-power, as in Gaschütz's theorem) that is not a conjugation map (φ ∉ Inn(G)); the non-abelian hypothesis is essential and must be kept, and p ranges over all primes.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition: for every prime p and every finite group G with IsPGroup p G and ¬ IsMulCommutative G, there is φ : MulAut G with orderOf φ = p and φ not in the range of MulAut.conj (= Inn(G)). Verified: MulAut.conj g h = g * h * g⁻¹, so its range is exactly Inn(G); MulAut G is finite for finite G so orderOf φ = p means order exactly p (never the default 0), as the decomposition notes require (stronger than Gaschütz's p-power order); p.Prime is explicit and with [Finite G] IsPGroup p G ⟺ |G| = p^n; ¬ IsMulCommutative G excludes abelian (incl. trivial) groups, keeping the essential hypothesis. Non-vacuity checked (D₈ satisfies the hypotheses). Chose c08/c04's binder style with Type* and `φ ∉ MulAut.conj.range` (reads directly as φ ∉ Inn(G)); the final file is c08's declaration with the range written with an explicit type ascription as in c04, and a docstring following the source wording. The `∀ g, φ ≠ MulAut.conj g` / `¬ ∃ g, φ = MulAut.conj g` variants (c02, c03, c06, c07) are logically equivalent and would also have been acceptable.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.13

by Ya. G. Berkovich

Prove that every finite non-abelian $p$-group admits an automorphism of order $p$
which is not an inner one.

Here the inner automorphisms of $G$ are the conjugation maps $x \mapsto g x g^{-1}$
for $g \in G$, i.e. the range of `MulAut.conj : G →* MulAut G`. The automorphism is
required to have order exactly $p$ in $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.13»

/--
Let $p$ be a prime and let $G$ be a finite non-abelian $p$-group. Then $G$ admits an
automorphism $\varphi$ of order $p$ which is not an inner one, i.e.
$\varphi \in \operatorname{Aut}(G) \setminus \operatorname{Inn}(G)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.13» (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (hG : IsPGroup p G) (hG' : ¬ IsMulCommutative G) :
    ∃ φ : MulAut G, orderOf φ = p ∧ φ ∉ (MulAut.conj : G →* MulAut G).range := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.13»

items: 'p-group' is `IsPGroup p G` (every element has p-power order) together with `p.Prime` and `[Finite G]`; for finite groups this is equivalent to |G| being a power of p.
'Non-abelian' is `¬ IsMulCommutative G`, which unfolds to ¬ ∀ a b, a * b = b * a; this excludes the trivial group and all abelian p-groups, as the source requires.
'Inner automorphism' is membership in `MulAut.conj.range`, the image of the conjugation homomorphism G →* MulAut G; `φ ∉ MulAut.conj.range` is 'φ is not inner'.
'Automorphism of order p' is `orderOf φ = p` in the group `MulAut G`, i.e. order exactly p (not merely p-power order as in Gaschütz's theorem).
The statement is universe-polymorphic (`G : Type*`) with hypotheses as theorem arguments, since the problem is an assertion rather than a question; no `answer(sorry)` is used.
Sanity check performed (not in file): the hypotheses are jointly satisfied by the dihedral group of order 8, so the statement is not vacuous.

reviewer_notes: Single-slot problem; the statement is an assertion ('Prove that …'), so it is stated as a plain theorem without answer(sorry), consistent with CONTRIBUTING.md. 'Order p' is read as the order of φ in Aut(G) (the standard reading; all candidates agree). No candidate omitted the slot; no decomposition objections were raised, and I concur. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning and also passes `lake --wfail build` when placed at FormalConjectures/Kourovka/4_13.lean.
